name: SWF World Championship
epitaph: Decided in a giant double-elimination tournament at the SWF's own first pay-per-view in May 1997; carried by Mr. Shhh during his run through Trinity, The Gangstas and The Church of Pain, and by Fatal Fury on the site's own last-dated (21 June 2000) champions page.

name: SWF Toughman Championship
epitaph: Crowned in a battle-royal format at the fed's own Birthday Blast anniversary show in 1998; held by Mark Adams on the site's own last-dated (21 June 2000) champions page.

name: SWF Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: One of the wing's own recurring singles titles across its run, changing hands among wrestlers including Pagan and Black Jack; held by E-Klipse on the site's own last-dated (21 June 2000) champions page.

name: SWF Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: The wing's lighter-weight singles title, held by El Viento de Muerta on the site's own final-season roster page and by El Cid on its last-dated (21 June 2000) champions page.

name: SWF Television Championship
epitaph: A recurring midcard singles title first awarded during the wing's own first year; held by Steven Braver on the site's own last-dated (21 June 2000) champions page.

name: SWF Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Changed hands repeatedly among the wing's own late-era teams (The Kold Blooded Killaz, The Living Dead, The Sanitarium of Fear); held by The Union of Former Owners on the site's own last-dated (21 June 2000) rankings page.

name: SWF American Championship
epitaph: A founding-era singles title Pagan held three times across the wing's run; the site's own final-season roster page no longer lists a current holder.

name: SWF International Championship
epitaph: A founding-era singles title changing hands among wrestlers including The Judge, Sean "The Duke" McKenzie and Equalizer; the site's own final-season roster page no longer lists a current holder.
